clue.text: Drink up what he'd not drunk before church

indicators.note: drunk suggests the words are reeling about, so the letters of what he'd not are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sober until church time is urged to knock back their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' looks like an order to the drinker; it is the definition. 'drunk' makes DOWNTHEHAT, and 'before' places it ahead of the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery toast urging someone to swallow their drink in one go; the idiom means the same as 'drink up'.

clue.text: Has a dislike of exams -primarily of French

indicators.note: primarily means first in place, so the French word stands at the front

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of'
exams are tests

explanation.surface: A student loathes examinations, above all those in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or abhor something is a strong way of disliking it; the verb forms match.

clue.text: Protest march not to be considered

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
an idea that is out is ruled out, not to be considered

explanation.surface: Demonstrators are told their planned march is out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike in which workers leave their place of work is a form of protest.

clue.text: Derby date arranged in Paddington, perhaps

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Derby date are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The date of the Derby horse race is fixed at a London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London station where a race-day trip might be arranged; here it is Michael Bond's fictional character from Peru. The Derby is England's famous flat horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington, Michael Bond's duffel-coated character, is a well-known example of a stuffed toy of this cuddly kind.

clue.text: Shell soldier participating in the rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
participating in means the soldier sits inside the word the

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is hit by a shell while taking part in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell here is a racing boat, not ammunition. 'participating in' gives THGIE, read upwards because 'rising' sits in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is a light racing rowing boat, and the classic one carries a crew of oarsmen numbering this many.

clue.text: Roads ran almost up to military depot

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lanes are minor roads

indicators.note: almost means the word ran loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Roads ran nearly as far as an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves RA; 'up' reads the roads-plus-RA string from the foot of the down light, so the depot appears.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store or factory for weapons and ammunition, so a depot for the forces.

clue.text: Business in time makes money

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A firm that is on time turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in circulation make up a country's currency, its metal cash.

clue.text: Trustworthy, and still improving

explanation.surface: A reliable person who keeps getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honest and above board, and read literally it describes something rising and rising, still getting better.

clue.text: Cross, it's clear, showed the way

parts.note: nett, as in profit, is what remains clear after deductions
a guide who showed the way led

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed insists it was obvious who led the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated or annoyed is being cross; both are adjectives of temper.

clue.text: Out of breath — tell a joke about it

indicators.note: about means the joke goes around the telling

parts.note: a gag is a joke
to spin a yarn is to tell a story

explanation.surface: A breathless comedian is told to tell a joke about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tell a joke about it' as 'put a joke around the telling': 'it' refers back to 'tell', and 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting for air is struggling to catch their breath.

clue.text: Brunel's innovative form of transport — "Stagecoach"?

explanation.surface: The engineer Brunel's pioneering vehicle is compared to a stagecoach.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel engineered the railway from London to Bristol and the steamship of that name. Stagecoach is John Ford's classic 1939 cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel built the famous railway and transatlantic steamship of this name; a celebrated cowboy film such as Stagecoach is a fine example of the genre.

clue.text: The man's given a conservative account

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician gives his own version of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle or record of past events is an account of them.

clue.text: Things made of metal could deteriorate in water

indicators.note: could deteriorate means the letters of in water break down into a new order

explanation.surface: Metal objects may rust if left in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots, pans and other household goods made from tin plate are metal articles.

clue.text: 8 ahead, leading the series

definitions.note: 8 is the across answer meaning cross or annoyed

indicators.note: leading means this piece comes first

parts.note: a side that is ahead is up, as in two goals up
a set is a series of things belonging together

explanation.surface: A competitor is ahead, leading the series.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to clue 8, a word for annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put out or irritated, the sense of the answer to 8, is the same as being distressed or bothered.

clue.text: Used to soften millet — one foments it

indicators.note: foments means stirs up, so the letters of millet and one are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook softens millet grains while someone stirs the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing cream or lotion applied to make the skin supple is used for softening.

clue.text: Military command could be responsible for mad errors

indicators.note: could be means the letters of mad errors may be rearranged into another phrase

explanation.surface: An officer's order might cause wild blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill instruction telling soldiers to lower their rifles to rest beside the right foot is a parade-ground order.

clue.text: Flower from high priest upset Diana

parts.note: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first high priest of Israel

indicators.note: upset means the actress's surname is turned upside down

parts.note: Diana Dors was a glamorous British film actress of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers from a senior cleric offends a woman called Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall yellow-flowered mullein takes its name from the budding staff in the Book of Numbers; it is a plant in bloom.

clue.text: Some apparel I eventually replace

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some clothing will need replacing in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over from someone on duty is to stand in for them, as one sentry relieves another.

clue.text: Colourful lady cutting material up into quarters

indicators.note: into means the fabric is placed inside the compass letters

parts.note: north and south are two of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the fabric is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A brightly dressed woman cuts up cloth into four pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SERGE into EGRES, which goes 'into' N and S. The answer is a dated term now regarded as offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive word for a Black woman; 'colourful' alludes to skin colour in the usage of the time.

clue.text: Small creature without a tail — it resembles a gnat

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: midget is a dated word for a very small person or thing

explanation.surface: A tiny tailless animal looks rather like a gnat.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny two-winged biting fly is very like a gnat.

clue.text: It reminds me to infiltrate soldiers

indicators.note: infiltrate signals one piece slipping inside another; here the soldiers end up between me and to

parts.note: men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A note reminds the writer to slip in among the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, 'infiltrate' would put the pronoun-and-preposition inside the soldiers; the setter means the troops slip in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or souvenir is kept because it brings something back to mind.

clue.text: Soldier has to last for hours with nothing to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the phrase swallows the nought

parts.note: something that drags on goes on tediously for hours
O, the figure nought, means nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier must endure hours on end without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted infantryman in historical armies; the word now names a cavalry soldier.

clue.text: What is 500 + 4 ÷ 50 please?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed (scan confirms): 'What is 500 + 4 ÷ 50 please?' The answer needs D + EIGHT split by L (E-L-IGHT), i.e. 8 not 4; a numeral slip the setterError row cannot express.

clue.text: Master starts to teach under the old regime

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster begins teaching under a former government.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints at the Tudor regime, a near-twin of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher or college don is a master who instructs pupils.

clue.text: Ragged man wearing torn scrap of cloth

indicators.note: wearing means the man has the torn garment around him

parts.note: rent, from rend, means torn

indicators.note: ragged means the letters of man are tattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A tattered man in a ripped shirt holds a scrap of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' turns MAN into MNA, which RENT surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover end of a bolt of fabric is a small piece of material.

clue.text: Stage now under discussion

explanation.surface: A play is staged while the topic is being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a play is to stage it; the current moment is now; a matter being considered is the one in hand.

clue.text: Give voice to private spite

indicators.note: Give voice to means the word is spoken, so the answer sounds like it

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, a private

explanation.surface: Someone finally speaks out about a secret grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter, long-lasting resentment is malice or spite.

clue.text: With no work, under pressure to retire, it could make quite a stir

definitions.text: it could make quite a stir

indicators.note: to retire means to go back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a work
stressed means under pressure

explanation.surface: A stressed worker forced to retire might cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reverses the whole string at once, so the pressure word comes out as the sweet course with the spoon after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding utensil is used for stirring as well as eating, and is larger than a teaspoon.
